## Start with one concrete problem

**LeetCode 295 — Find Median from Data Stream.** An online sequence whose state is updated as new items arrive.

Before naming a data structure, imagine solving the problem by hand with four or five values. This topic is primarily a **representation**, not a single algorithm; the choice of representation changes which operations are cheap.

### The obvious method — and why it falls short

Keep all received values, resort the entire list after every insertion.

### The one insight to remember

An online algorithm preserves a compact state between arrivals. Two heaps can keep the smaller half and larger half so the median is available without full sorting.

## Build the mathematical meaning from a small example

$$
|\,|L|-|R|\,|\leq1
$$

**What each symbol means:** L is the multiset in the lower max-heap and R the upper min-heap; |L| and |R| are their sizes. The outer absolute value means the size difference is at most one.

**Substitute actual values:** After receiving 2,9,5, the lower heap can contain {2,5} and upper {9}. Their sizes are 2 and 1, differing by 1, and the median is max(L)=5.

Do not move to implementation until you can explain this example without reading the formula.

## Design the algorithm in ordinary English

1. State what the stored representation means before the first operation.
2. Perform exactly the operation suggested by the example, updating only the necessary state.
3. Check the invariant after the operation, especially on duplicates, boundaries and empty input.
4. Stop when the requested result is known; do not perform work unrelated to the output.

**Correctness argument (the invariant):** Maintain all lower values ≤ all upper values and keep size difference at most one. The middle element(s) are then exactly the heap root(s).

## Code you can run

This example is best understood as a tiny state transformation. Implement the operation described above in JavaScript or Java, and check each reference or invariant after every step; the exact code is deliberately not replaced by a large framework.

## Why it works, and how expensive it is

Maintain all lower values ≤ all upper values and keep size difference at most one. The middle element(s) are then exactly the heap root(s).

**Time and space:** O(log n) per insertion and O(1) median read using two heaps; n is number of observed values.

**Common mistake or limitation:** For streaming data, an algorithm that needs the entire final sequence before answering is an offline algorithm, not a truly online one.

## Try to explain it in an interview

Without looking at code, repeat the numerical example and answer: *What does the representation remember that the naive method repeatedly recomputes?* Then state one change in assumptions that would invalidate your chosen technique.
